findings.rationale: Migration output is computed from previously read contents, but the commit phase checks only file metadata before replacing each path. An edit made after planning is silently overwritten, and a multi-file run can destroy concurrent changes while reporting success. The writer must verify the current bytes or digest against the planned source immediately before committing.

Bounds from the new specification are applied to the old model only when the key also occurred in old_scope. If an existing type first gains an explicit bound in the new file, that bound is dropped for the old model, so the two models are compared under different domains even though the result claims comparison:"new". This can create or hide semantic-diff findings.

A scope change switches old-model loading from the path-aware load_model flow to parse_kernel_source_with_bounds, which receives neither the source path nor an FsResolver rooted at its parent. Consequently, valid old specifications with relative imports can fail or resolve differently only when scope changes.

Document generation renders an applied approval with target.reviewed_digest, whereas document checking reconstructs the same AppliedApproval with target.digest. These fields intentionally represent different artifacts, so a generated approved document can be reported drifted by document check even when the spec and approval record are unchanged.

approval_evaluation computes status from current spec, artifact, claim-set, and reviewed digests, but run_approval_check returns nonzero only for the special signature-invalid status. Any ordinary stale or drifted evaluation is emitted with exit code 0, allowing CI approval gates to pass after the approved inputs have changed.
